SMTO-PRX-0018 — SMTO couldn't find that VM on your Proxmox server

GUID: f2b20884-27a1-4c7c-8c22-0ece26ee7dae
Slug: proxmox-guest-not-found
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO looked through the VMs and containers on your Proxmox server and none matched the name or number you gave. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list the VMs on your Proxmox server, and check the exact name or ID number of the one you want. The name must match the one in Proxmox; only capital letters may differ.
  2. If you have more than one Proxmox server, make sure you mentioned the right one with @. A VM on a different server won't appear in this server's list.
  3. If the VM exists in Proxmox but isn't in the Agent's list, ask the person who manages Proxmox whether your account is allowed to see it. Proxmox only shows SMTO the VMs that the saved account has permission to see.

What success looks like

  • The Agent finds the VM and shows its status or completes the action.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Proxmox. Don't reuse an old VM name or number from memory; take it from a fresh list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Guest resolution found no QEMU/LXC entry in /cluster/resources matching the requested VMID or name.

What this means

  • Guest selection finds no inventory candidate matching the supplied name/identity. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • Guest selection finds no inventory candidate matching the supplied name/identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the selected profile, node, guest type and identifier against current inventory.

How to fix it

  • Re-read /cluster/resources?type=vm and compare node, name and VMID with the request. A missing guest can also mean the profile's account lacks VM.Audit on it, because PVE filters inventory by permission, or that the wrong Proxmox Server profile was selected.
  • Refresh inventory and correct the selected node and guest identifier.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing guest is selected from the correct server inventory.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
